questions.title: Explain how checksums detect accidental data corruption
questions.summary: Describe how a checksum helps a system detect that stored or transmitted data has been altered accidentally.
questions.expectation: A strong answer explains what a checksum is, when it is computed, what happens on mismatch, and why that indicates corruption rather than malicious attack.
questions.practicePrompt: Explain how checksums are used to detect accidental corruption when moving a large backup file between two servers.

examMetadata.stimulus: A network administrator moves a large backup file between two servers.

points: checksum value is generated before or during transfer
receiving system recalculates or compares the value
mismatch indicates accidental corruption or an altered file
answer links the check to backup-file integrity
indicativeMarkScheme.modelAnswerOutline: A strong answer explains how the checksum is generated, compared after transfer, and used to flag accidental corruption.

questions.title: Complete a test log after repairing a booking script
questions.summary: A small venue has repaired a Python booking script and now needs evidence that the repaired date and ticket-count checks work.
questions.expectation: A strong response gives test-log rows with test description, test data, expected outcome, actual outcome, and one sensible retest or intended action.
questions.practicePrompt: Complete test-log entries for the repaired booking script, including normal, boundary and erroneous data.

examMetadata.vocationalContext: A small venue uses a Python booking script for visit dates and ticket quantities.
examMetadata.stimulus: The repaired script needs testing evidence before handover.

points: test data includes normal, boundary and erroneous cases
expected and actual outcomes are specific
intended action or retest is recorded for any failed result
indicativeMarkScheme.modelAnswerOutline: A strong response produces realistic test-log evidence for the repaired defect rather than a generic testing definition.
